# Rhodiola rosea

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="rhodiola-rosea-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="rhodiola-rosea-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="rhodiola-rosea-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Rhodiola rosea in the HMI library has 50 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury and Co from 1 source.<sup class="cite">[[sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Porwollik S, Jafari M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">The quality and safety of Rhodiola rosea supplements on the U.S. market: An analysis of biomarkers, heavy metals, and pesticide residues</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS One</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury and Co, in 50 results from 1 source.<sup class="cite">[[sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Porwollik S, Jafari M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">The quality and safety of Rhodiola rosea supplements on the U.S. market: An analysis of biomarkers, heavy metals, and pesticide residues</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS One</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Form, basis and where the rhodiola rosea was sampled; reporting limits decide how many results are non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Porwollik S, Jafari M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">The quality and safety of Rhodiola rosea supplements on the U.S. market: An analysis of biomarkers, heavy metals, and pesticide residues</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS One</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Porwollik S, Jafari M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">The quality and safety of Rhodiola rosea supplements on the U.S. market: An analysis of biomarkers, heavy metals, and pesticide residues</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS One</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
</ul>
</section>

<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Rhodiola rosea in the HMI library has 50 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury and Co from 1 source.<sup class="cite">[[sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Porwollik S, Jafari M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">The quality and safety of Rhodiola rosea supplements on the U.S. market: An analysis of biomarkers, heavy metals, and pesticide residues</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS One</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the rhodiola rosea came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

## What counts as rhodiola rosea

This page covers rhodiola rosea, as sold (50 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Porwollik S, Jafari M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">The quality and safety of Rhodiola rosea supplements on the U.S. market: An analysis of biomarkers, heavy metals, and pesticide residues</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS One</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Results stay on the basis each source reports: as sold or fresh weight, dry weight, or unstated. Dry-weight, as-sold and unstated results are never pooled, and no moisture conversion is applied.

24 rows can be rated against an HMI reference for the same form and basis, 0 rows have a direct same-study comparison, and the rest stay unrated with the reason recorded.

Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤5</td><td>27.7</td><td>75.1</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤5</td><td>27.7</td><td>75.1</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>10 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Porwollik et al. 2026</td><td>10</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for rhodiola rosea, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Porwollik et al. 2026 is the only compatible sampling family for rhodiola rosea, as sold on this basis in the completed rhodiola rosea ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market" class="internal" data-slug="sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market" data-no-cite-meta>Porwollik et al. 2026</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:rhodiola-rosea-5e14eab6f0ae:c8719c2a1dac</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. (upper quartile).<sup class="cite">[[sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Porwollik S, Jafari M <a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Rhodiola rosea FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-rhodiola-rosea" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-rhodiola-rosea" data-question="What heavy metals are found in rhodiola rosea?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in rhodiola rosea?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury and Co in rhodiola rosea, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Porwollik S, Jafari M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">The quality and safety of Rhodiola rosea supplements on the U.S. market: An analysis of biomarkers, heavy metals, and pesticide residues</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS One</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-rhodiola-rosea-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-rhodiola-rosea-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of rhodiola rosea measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of rhodiola rosea measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 7 groups of rhodiola rosea ranged from 9 µg/kg (capsule product 3) to 88 µg/kg (capsule product 4); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Porwollik S, Jafari M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">The quality and safety of Rhodiola rosea supplements on the U.S. market: An analysis of biomarkers, heavy metals, and pesticide residues</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS One</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/porwollik2026-rhodiola-supplements-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
